title: Learn your first sounds
goal: One idea runs through all of lyk. Learn it, and the rest is vocabulary.

blocks.x: lyk is steno where **every stroke after the first of a word carries a join key (`+`)**. A stroke without it always starts a new word. Nothing has to be guessed from the keys.
The whole benefit in one key, the right-hand `D`:

head: You strike
It reads
Why
rows: No `+`, so it is a word: *do*.
The same `-D` with `+` is the ending *-ed*.
Without `+`, the same two strokes are two words.

blocks.x: Other theories give the ending `-D` (*-ed*) the key, so *do* cannot be one. Here the join key tells them apart, so a word and an ending can share a key. Many do:
So an ending can be a single key, with no extra keys or dropped vowels to keep it from being read as a word.

items: `/` separates the strokes of one word: [[WAUBG/+-G]].
`+` in front of a stroke is the join key, struck together with that stroke's other keys.
Keys always appear in **steno order**: `S T K P W H R`, then `A O * E U`, then `F R P B L G T S D Z`.
A `-` marks a stroke with only right-hand keys: [[-G]] is the G on the right, not on the left.

blocks.x: Every word has exactly **one primary** one-stroke outline, the one this course teaches. Extra outlines exist, but they only take strokes nobody else needs, so you never have to choose.
Try the board: strike keys together on your keyboard or steno machine. Q is the join key.

items: **Board and sounds (lessons 2 to 7).** Learn where each sound lives. Drill until a chord comes out without thinking.
**Common words (8 and 9).** A few hundred briefs cover most of what you type. They are memorised, not derived.
**The join key (10 to 13).** Endings, prefixes, syllables. This is how you type any word you have not memorised, so you are never stuck.
**Beyond words (14 to 16).** Phrases, punctuation, commands, letters.
**Practice (17 and 18).** Edge cases, then a daily routine.

blocks.x: Each lesson is short on purpose. Read it, point at the strokes, do the **drill** at the bottom. A drill passes at 90% right on the first try; your best score is saved in this browser.

This site reads an ordinary keyboard the way Plover's QWERTY mode does: hold the keys of a stroke together, then let go. The home row and the row above it are the consonants, `C V` and `N M` the vowels, `T G` and `Y H` the star, and **`Q` is the join key** (the `+` above `S-`, as on a Keymux board).
On a real steno keyboard, use the dictionary files this project builds (see the main README) and bind your own key to `+`.

blocks.q: Which one starts a new word?
blocks.why: Only a stroke without the join key begins a word.
